messages.content: You are the Appeals Chamber clerk-agent assigned to prepare the Chamber’s review of appealed findings. Your standing duty is to assess the record and the Trial Chamber’s stated reasons, keep the distinction between record evidence and appellate inference clear, and produce a reasoned disposition for the Chamber. Follow the Chamber’s rules of procedure and do not add facts to the record. You deal with the Presiding Judge, the Appeals Registrar, the Evidence Unit, and counsel through the appeal docket. Tools: docket.lookup retrieves filings and docket entries; evidence.search retrieves indexed record material; schedule.status checks hearing and filing calendar entries; log.write records administrative notes. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: appeals-registrar
messages.content: Morning docket handover: the review file is open under the Storm appeals tab. The hearing room allocation remains unchanged, and the registry has received the final pagination check from both language desks. The clerk’s note says the parties’ submissions and the trial materials are indexed; the annex scan from the western filing counter is still awaiting a legibility check. Please use the record references rather than relying on the hearing-room bundle, which is missing two divider sheets. The Presiding Judge’s office has asked that any short administrative note be logged before the end of the morning session.

messages.name: docket.lookup
messages.content:
Docket extract / registry copy

Appeal file status: materials indexed; pagination review complete. The panel’s working bundle carries the ordinary exhibit cross-reference sheet. A duplicate photocopy of the hearing schedule has a faint stamp at the lower edge; no filing deadline is recorded on that page.

Reasons digest, issue heading: Four Towns artillery. The Trial Chamber treated the Four Towns artillery as unlawful, and its reasons leaned heavily on the impact assessment. The judgment uses one artillery-error allowance throughout, but identifies no record material from which that figure was drawn. The paragraph references point to the impact tables and the general discussion of artillery accuracy; no source note accompanies the allowance itself.

The next docket entry concerns a translation correction in a separate appeal. The translator’s note changes a comma in a quotation and has no effect on the exhibit numbering. Registry staff have not yet replaced the paper copy in the outer binder. Counsel’s filing receipts are complete, and the electronic copy opens normally.

messages.name: appeals-counsel-liaison
messages.content: The duty counsel from the appellate team has been checking the hearing bundle against the electronic record. Their view, offered informally, is that the Chamber should use the vacatur route; they say the unexplained allowance is difficult to square with the range of accuracy testimony. The liaison also asked whether the paragraph cross-references are stable, since the paper bundle’s tabs were inserted after the first pagination pass. No revised filing has come in since the registry’s morning check.

messages.name: appeals-registrar
messages.content:
ATTACHED DOCUMENT — Registry note on the Trial Judgment, circulated with the record index

For the artillery issue, the Chamber stated its conclusion in the reasons section and referred the reader to the impact discussion. The attached index gives the paragraph range and the exhibit numbers; it does not supply a separate technical source for the allowance appearing in the impact discussion. The paper index uses roman numerals, while the electronic index uses the paragraph numbers printed in the judgment. Both point to the same portion of the record.

The reviewing panel may sustain the conclusion that the Four Towns shelling violated the law, keeping that determination in the judgment. This sentence records a procedural route in the appellate framework; it is not a view on how the evidence should be assessed.

In discussing one attack, the Trial Chamber called it disproportionate, yet supplied no concrete weighing of expected military gain against harm and made no determination of resulting damage or casualties. The Brioni Transcript was among the admitted materials; the reasons on the character of the artillery attacks do not cite it expressly. The index places that transcript among the conference materials, between a map register and a stenographer’s correction sheet. The correction sheet concerns a misheard place name in a different session.

The note was prepared to reconcile the exhibit list with the paragraph index. It does not alter either document. The binding desk reports a slight curl on the upper-right corner of several photocopies, but all text remains legible. The appeal file’s cover sheet carries the standard blue registry stamp.

messages.name: evidence.search
messages.content:
Evidence Unit retrieval / 08:46

Hearing transcript, artillery accuracy segment: The gunnery witnesses spoke from narrow test conditions; their distance remarks pointed to poorer precision farther out, and their estimates did not match. One witness was asked about a range used during training; another described a different setting. The transcript index labels this section “technical background,” not a finding of the Trial Chamber.

Operational reporting bundle, Knin references: There were indications that police or army vehicles may have crossed Knin while the shelling was underway. The source lines are intermittent; two entries give no time stamp and one uses an abbreviated unit label. A map sheet in the same envelope has a torn edge but its grid is intact.

Observation section, record summary: On whether crews could see possible targets in Knin at the material times, the evidence did not settle the point. The summary does not characterize the issue as resolved in either direction. A witness schedule attached to the section includes a lunch break notation and an interpreter handover.

Fire-report extract: Several entries appear to direct fire toward largely civilian districts without naming a particular target; the returns are incomplete and wording remains ambiguous. The bundle contains a routing cover, two clipped forms, and a later index card that does not identify who prepared it. Some of the handwritten marks are faint. The Evidence Unit has not normalized the abbreviations in this extract, and the page sequence follows the original envelope rather than the hearing order.

The retrieval system found no additional page under the exact search phrase. One duplicate item is filed under the general operations heading. The record clerk has left a note that its scan is rotated by a quarter turn; the text can still be read on screen.

messages.name: appeals-registrar
messages.content: Routine check: the morning conference room has been returned to the registry pool. The facilities desk is asking whether the spare lectern microphone should remain on the booking sheet for next week; no response is needed from the panel on that item. The filing counter will close for its scheduled inventory at 12:30, and the courier tray is due for collection shortly before then.

messages.name: schedule.status
messages.content: Calendar status: the morning conference-room booking has been released to the registry pool. The next listed internal block is the usual document review period. No new hearing notice or filing alert has been entered since the last synchronization. Facilities has not added the spare microphone to next week’s booking sheet. This is an administrative status response; no action is pending in the calendar queue.
